newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel down on India's low import.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel down on India's low import.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices fell on talk that state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) took only 90,000 tonnes in two cargoes in its tender for September delivery, traders said on Friday.
This was much lower than the 200,000-300,000 tonnes that the market had anticipated earlier and was expected to send bearish ripples through the market next week. India took 165,000 tonnes in August.
Traders said IOC awarded both cargoes to the east coast at around 47 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight basis, to Shell and Cargill each.
But parties named in the tender said they expect IOC to confirm the award later this evening or on Saturday.
The softer sentiment on Singapore gas oil market were seen even earlier after it had hit the near-term peak of $22.85 per barrel and was testing the $23.00-mark, traders said on Friday.
They said expectation of a resurgence in Chinese buying has not yet materialised. This together with India's low award has put a damper on the earlier buoyant market.

Gas oil prices have gained $3.00 over the last three weeks after hitting a low of $19.85, and traded at $22.85 on Tuesday. Since then, sellers were trying to test the $23.00-mark but buyers stayed away as regional demand outlets were unclear.

On Friday, three sellers appeared at $22.80, free-on-board (fob) basis, 15 cents below Thursday's offers, but buyers remained aloof and their nervousness were proven to a certain extent by India's small award.

But demand has emerged from Nepal in September. It has issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil for September 21-30 delivery. The tender will close on August 13, traders said.
Amid the bearish near-term outlook, some traders said supplies in the MidEast are tight up to mid-August.
They said this could be the reason why fewer MidEast gas oil supplies are heading to East Asia.

Swaps gas oil values also fell as sellers emerged in force on sentiment that the market has been overbought. August lost 50 cebnts to be last quoted at $22.45/$22.55, while September 30 cents to be last indicated at $23.15/$23.25.
Jet fuel was offered higher with three sellers indicating at $23.00 per barrel for mid-August, fob.
Traders said the market was in steep contango as oil companies and traders stock up supplies in anticipation of healthy winter demand.
